newsitem.title: UK: Gold falls, base metals mute gains, wheat is firm.
newsitem.headline: Gold falls, base metals mute gains, wheat is firm.

text.p: Gold slumped on Thursday to its lowest in almost two years while volatile commodity markets also saw a rally in base metals pause but wheat prices remain firm.
Gold faced heavy selling pressure and slid to a low at $375.70 per ounce before closing in London at $376.65. Dealers expected further losses.
"The gold price is very disappointing. It wasn't able to break above $380 yesterday, even though normally this is a strong time of year for gold..." a London-based dealer said.
Sentiment in the gold market has been increasingly bearish in recent days after a rally last week ran out of steam at a peak of just under $385 an ounce.
Several base metals looked set on upward trends but copper turned sluggish and news that a major player was pulling out of floor dealing on the London Metal Exchange hurt sentiment.
Copper, the LME flagship contract, sagged back to support and closed at around $2,212.5 a tonne.
"Copper is overbought, the market is nervous and volumes are thin," a trader said.

Copper had hit a new five-month peak at 2,240-a-tonne on Wednesday, extending a rally that began late last week. Prices were boosted largely by data suggesting that stocks were at their lowest in six years.
Traders however reported market talk that the long run of inventory declines, which has brought LME copper stocks to the lowest since June 1990, may be coming to an end.
News late Wednesday that Lehman Brothers is to wind down its metals and energy business and relinquish LME ring dealer status made the market jittery at the opening.
It is the latest and largest adjustment on the metals market since the Sumitomo copper scandal erupted in June.
Other metal companies have cut staff numbers and bonus payments but Lehman is the first firm to stop trading on the market floor, trade sources said.
Aluminium, used for construction and transportation parts, continued Wednesday gains and tested $1,520-a-tonne resistance.
But it was just easier at $1,510 at the London close after news that the International Primary Aluminium Institute (IPAI) reported a year-on-year increase in third quarter 1996 alumina production.
Provisional IPAI figures show that total alumina production in the third was 10.178 million tonnes, up from 9.979 million tonnes in the same period.
Benchmark Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) wheat futures were again firm, at almost $4.20 per bushel, on signs of dwindling U.S. wheat stocks in deliverable locations.
London wheat futures also jumped following the result of the European Union (EU) weekly grain tender.
The EU granted 311,300 tonnes of free-market soft wheat 16.5 Ecus a tonne rebate.
In the soft commodities, cocoa futures ran into the sterling barrier after a fierce rally on Wednesday.
Benchmark March cocoa fell slightly to 925 pounds sterling a tonne at close after bouncing a stiff downtrend on Wednesday.
March white sugar contract managed to retain some of the upside momentum seen yesterday but activity was extremely light before the open of the New York raws market andit eased later.
IPE Brent futures added to early gains and tested upside resistance in later trade but failed to make up losses seen on Wednesday.
